trans.sense: somewhat indignant, irritated, angry, put out or annoyed

examples.text: I was miffed at Rick for his behavior. I was miffed at the coach, not for his naivete of deafness, but for his arrogance, which converted his ignorance to stupidity.
examples.ref: 2003, Jim Brewington, Let There Be Light Please!, →ISBN, page 130:

examples.text: And also, it's generally not a good idea to prank someone who's already miffed at you.
examples.ref: 2018, Josh Scorcher, Taking "28 Pranks Later" too Seriously:

examples.text: Donors might be miffed to find that a magnificent gift was not earmarked for rescue.
examples.ref: 2021 November 27, “In preparing for disasters, museums face tough choices”, in The Economist:

raw_glosses: (informal) Somewhat indignant, irritated, angry, in a snit, put out or annoyed.
glosses: Somewhat indignant, irritated, angry, in a snit, put out or annoyed.

examples.text: he [our Interpreter Shabonah] will not agree to work let our Situation be what it may nor Stand a guard, and if miffed with any man he wishes to return when he pleases
examples.ref: 1805 March 12, Bernard DeVoto, editor, The journals of Lewis and Clark, Houghton Mifflin, Boston, 1953, Clark's journal, page 85:

examples.text:
1824, Sir Walter Scott, Redgauntlet
[…] answered my Thetis, a little miffed perhaps -- to use the women's phrase — that I turned the conversation upon my former partner, rather than addressed it to herself.

1911, James Oliver Curwood, Philip Steele of the Royal Northwest Mounted Police
"Don't get miffed about it, man," returned Nome with an irritating laugh.

raw_glosses: (transitive, usually used in the passive) To offend slightly.

examples.text: I amble on; yet, though I know not why, / So sad I am!—but should a friend and I / Grow cool and miff, O! I am very sad!
examples.ref: c. 1797, Samuel Taylor Coleridge, “To Simplicity”, in Sonnets Attempted in the Manner of Contemporary Writers:

examples.text:
1905, George Barr McCutcheon, Jane Cable
She miffed and started to reply, but thought better of it.
